newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda, Ford to share engines from 1999 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mazda, Ford to share engines from 1999 - paper.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp and Ford Motor Co have agreed to share engines in the hope of cutting development costs, a Japanese business daily reported on Thursday.
A spokesman for Mazda was not immediately available to comment on the Nihon Keizai Shimbun report.
Under the scheme, Mazda will develop engines for small vehicles and Ford will do the same for larger cars, the paper said.
Mazda will develop an in-line 4-cylinder model with a displacement of 1,800-2,000cc as the first engine to be developed under the scheme, the paper said.
The new engine will be used to power a sports-utility vehicle, which is expected to be manufactured at Ford's Lorain, Ohio, plant from 1999, the paper said.
